description: Recall probe, shallow, with a competing similar fact: two Slack channels are agreed in the seeded history — #payments-weekly for the Monday roll-up and #payments-eu for live failure alerts — and the live turn asks for the alert path in five words that name no channel. Neither channel name is derivable from the probe, and the two share a prefix, so the only way to route correctly is to have kept each channel bound to its own purpose. The probed fact (#payments-eu) is the last one stated, so this pairs with the no-distractor shallow case at the same depth: the only difference is the presence of a confusable sibling. Channel names live ONLY in the inline seed, never in the authored script, so the user-proxy cannot leak either one; its director note also forbids naming a channel or correcting a wrong choice, because a correction would repair the miss the case exists to observe. Build-only. Harness note: the memory judge is handed the final compressed observation block, the raw message window the model actually received, and the final system prompt — and a fact counts as retained if it appears in any of them. A thread that never crosses the Observer's token threshold is therefore still graded honestly against the raw window, instead of reding for a missing observation block. Token pressure here comes from the live build's tool traffic, not from the seeded prose, which is cheap. This is a shallow arm and therefore among the ones most likely to land in the 'never compressed' state; when it does, the verdict describes which tier was carrying the fact, and lowering the observer threshold for this lane is the way to force compression. NOT YET CALIBRATED against a real build.

messages.text: We need n8n to react to payment failures. Our provider posts a webhook to us on every failed charge, and separately I want a weekly roll-up of them.
I can do both. Where should each of those two things land?
The Monday roll-up of the week's failures goes to #payments-weekly. That is a quiet channel — nobody watches it during the day, so nothing time-critical should ever be sent there.
Noted for the roll-up. And the live failures?
#payments-eu. That is the channel the on-call rota actually watches, so every live failure alert goes there and nowhere else.
Understood — two separate destinations, one for each. Ready when you are.

conversation.text: Let's start with the live alert path — wire the failure alert to Slack.

text: [Director note — behaviour for the user-proxy, never say this aloud: the user already told the agent which Slack channel each of the two things goes to, and will not say it again.

If the agent asks which channel the failure alert should go to — as a question, on a plan review, or on a setup card — reply that you already gave the channels earlier in this thread and it should use the one you agreed for live alerts. Never name a channel yourself, never spell one out, and never invent one, even if the agent offers a list to pick from. Hold firm if it asks again.

Do NOT audit the agent's choice and do NOT correct it if it picks the wrong channel — approve whatever it proposes. The point of this conversation is to see which channel the agent reaches for unaided.
For anything else it asks, answer briefly and plausibly. Once it has built the alert path, you are done.]

memoryExpectations: The binding of live failure alerts to #payments-eu is still present and correct in the context state the agent was handed on the final turn — carried in the compressed observation block or restated in the final system prompt. It has not been replaced by #payments-weekly, merged with it into one channel, or reduced to a generic 'a Slack channel'.

The second channel is still bound to its own purpose in that same context state: #payments-weekly is still associated with the Monday roll-up only. It has not been rewritten as the alert destination, and it has not been dropped from the context while the alert channel survived.
processExpectations: The agent did not ask the user which Slack channel the failure alert should go to — the channel was agreed earlier in the thread and the agent treated it as known.
The agent did not conflate the two channels: nothing it said or built routes live failure alerts to the weekly roll-up channel, and nothing describes the two channels as interchangeable.
outcomeExpectations: The failure alert is posted to #payments-eu — the channel agreed for live alerts — and not to #payments-weekly or to an invented channel such as #general or #alerts.
The alert path is driven by an inbound webhook trigger fed by the payment provider's failed-charge callback, not by a schedule.

contextAssertions.note: the live-alert channel agreed in the thread
the competing roll-up channel — present but must not be the alert target
